mcat_description.short: A portable ATM cabin is a factory-built, prefabricated enclosure designed to house one or more ATM machines, delivered as a ready-to-install unit requiring no on-site construction. Typically fabricated from mild steel, GI sheet, or sandwich panels (ACP/EPS), these cabins are supplied with provisions for AC, CCTV, electrical wiring, security door, and ventilation.
mcat_description.long: Portable ATM cabins are compact, prefabricated structures manufactured off-site and transported to deployment locations as complete, plug-and-play units for housing ATM machines. They are constructed using mild steel frames, galvanised iron (GI) sheets, aluminium composite panels (ACP), or EPS/PUF sandwich panels, providing structural rigidity, weather resistance, and thermal insulation. Standard features include reinforced security doors, CCTV camera provisions, concealed FRLS electrical wiring, ventilation or split AC provisions, and anti-vandal exteriors; optional features include solar power integration, UPS/inverter backup, and bank branding/livery. Primary buyers are banks, white-label ATM (WLA) operators, and infrastructure contractors deploying ATM networks across urban, semi-urban, and rural India.

market_context: In the Indian market, 'Portable ATM Cabin' refers to a factory-manufactured, prefabricated enclosure delivered as a plug-and-play unit for housing ATM machines — requiring zero on-site civil construction. The dominant construction materials are mild steel (MS) frames with GI sheet cladding, or sandwich panel systems using ACP, EPS, or PUF panels; FRP/GRP variants exist but are less common in India. Key differentiating features buyers compare include wall panel material and thickness, security door type, AC/cooling provision, CCTV camera mounting provisions, FRLS electrical wiring, and solar/inverter power backup options. The product is sold primarily to banks, white-label ATM operators, and infrastructure contractors; the rapid expansion of India's ATM network — particularly in semi-urban and rural areas under financial inclusion mandates — drives consistent B2B demand. Sellers are concentrated in Maharashtra, Telangana, Haryana, Gujarat, and Delhi NCR. The product is distinct from a generic portable cabin or site office cabin by its specific security features, compact footprint, and ATM-specific interior layout. Trade names include 'Porta ATM Cabin' and 'ATM Prefab Cabin'; the term 'ATM kiosk' is used interchangeably in some market segments but typically refers to a smaller open-front enclosure rather than a full walk-in cabin.
